data: Russia's northern military cosmodrome — over 1,500 launches by 1997, more than any other site

Fleet launch-site entry for the whole Plesetsk Cosmodrome (until 2026-10-21 it covered only pad 41/1; the id is kept for its URLs). Founded in 1957 as an R-7 ICBM base; first orbital launch Kosmos 112 on 17 March 1966 from Site 41/1; more than 1,500 launches by 1997. Pads: 41/1, 16/2 and 43 (R-7 family), 132 and 133 (Kosmos-3M, Rokot), 32 (Tsyklon-3), 35 (Angara, since 2014). Site 43 has its own entry. Sources: Wikipedia, Plesetsk Cosmodrome; Russian Space Web.
Russia's northern military cosmodrome — more launches than any other site

Plesetsk Cosmodrome lies in Russia's far north, at about 62.9°N. It was founded in 1957 as an R-7 intercontinental-missile base and became a space launch site on 17 March 1966, when a Vostok-2 rocket put Kosmos 112 into orbit from Site 41/1. Run by the Russian Ministry of Defence, it launched most Soviet military satellites — reconnaissance, navigation, early-warning and Molniya communications — and by 1997 had made more than 1,500 launches, more than any other site in the world. R-7 family rockets flew from Sites 41/1, 16/2 and 43; Kosmos-3M and Rokot from Sites 132 and 133; Tsyklon-3 from Site 32; and, since 2014, Angara from Site 35. Site 43 has its own entry.
